chapter: Fletcher Henderson and forming his own band
title: Why everyone wanted to play with Henderson
summary: The Henderson band was THE band to musicians of the day, with Smith, Hawkins, Redman and Bailey.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Okay. Then of course, you were with Fletcher at some time, even as late as 1934, I believe, weren't you?
Not even just for recording dates?
No, not that I remember. No.
Oh, I see. It must have been earlier then.

Well anyway, this brings us, really, to what we must come to -- and that is this question of -- which you alluded to eluded to earlier, that for a musician, it was an honor and an important thing to be invited to play with Fletcher Henderson's band.
Did you feel that at that time, in exactly that way -- or is that something we all think about in retrospect?
No. I felt that way because that was, to the musicians around town at that time, this was THE band, you know?

You know, we all used to listen to Henderson records, and you know, it sounded all very exciting. Joe Smith, that wonderful trumpet player, and Coleman Hawkins and Don Redman and Buster Bailey on the clarinet. Oh, we just loved this band, you know. Everybody wanted to play with Fletcher Henderson.
So it was something that you appreciated being invited to to, even at that very moment.
